events.event: BEI began excluding 81 high-shareholding-concentration (HSC) stocks from the IHSG calculation on 2 November, and the IHSG closed up 0.79% at 5,096.83 after dipping below 5,000 early in the session.
events.key_numbers: IHSG 5,096.83 (+39.78 pts, +0.79%) · 81 HSC stocks removed, ~18% of IHSG weight, ~30% of market cap · 837 stocks still counted · value ~Rp10.07 T (CNBC) · intraday low in the 4,980s, high above 5,120
events.why_it_matters: The index people watch now measures a different basket, so the IHSG number is no longer comparable with before 2 November.
events.spreading_evidence: Multiple CNBC Indonesia items on the HSC exclusion on 2 Nov; Bisnis, Kontan, Investortrust, Media Indonesia all covered it

events.event: After the HSC exclusion, index weights shifted to big banks and blue chips: CNBC lists BBRI at about 9%, BBCA 7.93%, BMRI up from 5.70% to 7.12%, TLKM up from 3.76% to 4.68%, and ASII up from 3.35% to 4.15%.
events.why_it_matters: Shows concretely who gains weight when the 'opaque' stocks leave the index, a clear chart for viewers who hold index funds.
events.spreading_evidence: CNBC Indonesia market headline 'bobotnya makin jumbo' (2 Nov)

events.event: BPS reported October 2026 inflation of 0.22% month on month and 3.23% year on year, driven mainly by red chili and other food prices, slightly below the 0.24% / 3.25% poll consensus.
events.key_numbers: m/m 0.22% · y/y 3.23% · year-to-date 2.4% · core y/y 2.56% · volatile food m/m 0.77%, y/y 5.81% · IHK 112.31 to 112.56 · red chili contribution 0.13 pt · highest region South Papua 1.12% m/m · North Sulawesi 8.07% y/y · target 2.5% ±1%
events.why_it_matters: Chili and food prices are what households feel first, and inflation matters for whether BI can hold rates at the 17-18 Nov meeting.
events.spreading_evidence: Covered by Kontan, Kumparan, Okezone, Suara, Investortrust on 2 Nov

events.event: BPS reported a September 2026 trade surplus of US$3.36 billion, well above the roughly US$1.0-1.8 billion that three economists had forecast, with imports (+18.41% y/y) growing faster than exports (+11.87% y/y).
events.key_numbers: surplus US$3.36 B (Aug US$3.55 B; Sep 2025 US$4.55 B) · exports US$27.59 B (+11.87% y/y) · imports US$24.23 B (+18.41% y/y) · oil and gas imports US$3.27 B (+23.94%) · copper exports +165.97% y/y · economist forecasts US$1.00-1.79 B
events.why_it_matters: A bigger dollar surplus is a cushion for the rupiah, but surging oil imports show where the pressure comes from.
events.spreading_evidence: CNBC 'Breaking News' item; Antara, Kontan, Katadata, Kumparan, Suara all covered

events.event: The rupiah closed weaker again on 2 November, near the record-low zone, while foreign investors kept selling Indonesian stocks.
events.key_numbers: Rp18,156/USD (OWRITE, -9 pts, -0.05%) · Rp18,140 (CNBC Indonesia video headline) · record close Rp18,183 on 28 Oct (Kontan) · JISDOR Rp18,139 on 27 Oct · foreign net sell YTD ~Rp97.92 T through 30 Oct (Legawa)
events.why_it_matters: A weak rupiah raises prices of imported goods, fuel and overseas tuition; vendors quote different closes, so cite the source.
events.spreading_evidence: Daily CNBC/Bisnis/Kontan rupiah close items; CNBC video headline 'rupiah nears Rp18,200'

events.event: OJK's capital-market regulation head Agus Firmansyah said MSCI's proposed downgrade to Standalone stems mainly from continuing concern about market dysfunction even after announced reforms, citing past cases involving BREN, CUAN and DSSA.
events.key_numbers: statement made 31 Oct 2026 · MSCI consultation feedback deadline 30 Apr 2027 (storyline)
events.why_it_matters: Explains in the regulator's words why a foreign index provider is worried, which drives foreign selling.

events.event: BPS is expected to release Q3 2026 GDP growth in the first week of November (exact date not confirmed), with economists projecting about 5.2-5.4% year on year.
events.key_numbers: GREAT Institute projection 5.2-5.4% y/y · InFast projection 5.4% · other economists 'above 5%' · date unconfirmed
events.why_it_matters: The headline growth number tests the 'economy is fine' claim against a 40%-plus fall in the IHSG this year.

events.event: US midterm elections take place on 3 November, with Indonesian market commentary watching the effect on the dollar and rate expectations after the Fed held at 3.75-4.00% with two dissenters favouring a hike.
events.key_numbers: Fed funds 3.75-4.00% (held 28 Oct) · 2 dissents for +25 bp (Cook, Hammack) · next FOMC 8-9 Dec · US CPI 3.7% y/y (Sep) · Brent ~US$114 on 27 Oct · BI RDG 17-18 Nov
events.why_it_matters: A possible December Fed hike plus high oil keeps pressure on the rupiah and limits room for BI to cut.
events.spreading_evidence: CNBC Indonesia video 'Effects on rupiah and IHSG if Fed raises rates'

events.event: Indonesian 10-year government bond yields rose to about 7.64% on 30 October, after touching 7.71% on 29 October, following a weak SUN auction on 27 October.
events.key_numbers: 10Y SBN yield ~7.64% (30 Oct) · peak 7.71% (29 Oct), highest since May 2020 per Trading Economics · SUN auction 27 Oct: bids Rp31.1 T (-52.1%), awarded Rp20.7 T vs target Rp30 T
events.why_it_matters: Higher government bond yields mean the state pays more to borrow and can push up mortgage and loan rates.
